port.plugTitle: Plug a connected cable into this port: first the cable from the wall (switch), then the cord to a device
port.allTitle: Gives every port the same tag, e.g. one VLAN (replaces their tags); then change single ports by clicking them. Empty — removes all tags
port.allClear: Remove the tags of all ports?
dev.hostnameTitle: Host name of the computer; shown on the plan and in cable routes when the item has no label
dev.badMac: Doesn't look like a MAC address (e.g. 3C:52:82:1A:2B:3C)
dev.badIp: Doesn't look like an IP address (e.g. 192.168.1.20 or 10.0.0.5/24)
port.tagTitle: Port tag: uplink, trunk, VLAN 10… (a plain number = VLAN). Shown on the switch, in the port list and in the routes of cables plugged in here
port.noLoose: All connected cables already have a port
port.faceHint: Click a port to choose the cable plugged into it; coloured = taken (cable colour), red frame = two cables in one port or beyond the port count
port.noCables: No cables are connected to this item yet — put a cable end on it
port.pick: Cable in this port (choose one of the cables connected to this item)
port.select: Port of the switch this end is plugged into; each port shows what is in it or that it is free
port.countTitle: Number of ports (switch, patch panel). Empty — from the catalog name
cable.inTray: In trays: Tidy routes the cable through the trays and the trays list it. Off — the cable runs on its own (e.g. under the ceiling)
desk.frameTitle: Metal frame under the desktop: distance from the desk edge (cm). Patch cords on the desk are fixed to it and leave at its corner (a patch cord button or Tidy lays them). Empty on a desk — 5 cm
cable.patchTitle: Patch cord: a ready-made cord of a standard length (1, 2, 3, 5, 10 m); the label shows the length you need, a free end shows a plug
cable.heightTitle: Height above the floor of the points that have no own height (cm)
cable.noCeiling: Set the room height in Wiring settings first
cable.pointsHint: Height of each point above the floor, cm (empty = from the item, tray or run height; grey = the height used). Between two heights the cable goes up or down.
cable.fixedOn: Route fixed: Tidy leaves this cable as it is (set by itself when you drag, add or remove its points). Click to let Tidy lay it again
cable.fixedOff: Fix the route: Tidy will leave this cable as it is
cable.simplify: Remove extra points: on a straight line, repeated, back-and-forth spikes (points with an own height or a connector stay). A point can also be removed with Alt + click, a double-click or by dropping it onto its neighbour
elev.label: Height
elev.item: Mounting height above the floor (cm): connected cables come in here. Empty — the height of the tray the item stands in
elev.tray: Height above the floor (cm): cables run at this height while in the tray; sockets standing in the tray take it too
cable.notLinked: Not connected — put the end on a socket or switch
action.tidyTitle: Lay out the cables neatly: right angles, close parallel runs merged into one, runs near a tray put on it; fixed routes (lock) stay (Ctrl+Z undoes)
chain.title: The whole cable: start → consumers in order, total length
chain.continue: Continue the cable from a point
joint.add: Connectors: click the cable where two cables are joined (extended); click a connector again to remove it
joint.pick: Click the cable to put a connector (again — remove it). A click elsewhere or Esc — done
chain.attach: Attach to another cable (this one becomes its continuation)
chain.detach: Detach: make it a separate cable
chain.pickContinue: Click the point on the cable to continue from (Esc — cancel)
chain.pickAttach: Click the cable to attach to (Esc — cancel)

help.title: Quick help
help.select.title: Select tool:
help.select.text: click furniture or text to select, drag to move, drag handles to resize/rotate. Drag wall nodes and ruler ends to reshape.
help.wall.title: Draw walls:
help.wall.text: Wall tool → drag from point to point; keep dragging from the last point to continue. Tap to finish the chain.
help.split.title: Split wall:
help.split.text: Wall tool → click on an existing wall.
help.exterior.title: Exterior wall:
help.exterior.text: right-click a wall to toggle exterior / interior.
help.lengths.title: Wall lengths:
help.lengths.text: “Inside” shows the length of each wall measured inside the room; “Both” adds the outside; “Axis” shows centre-line lengths.
help.measure.title: Ruler:
help.measure.text: drag between two points to measure; ends snap to walls and furniture, Shift keeps the line straight. Measurements stay on the plan; remove them with Erase.
help.text.title: Text:
help.text.text: Text tool → click to add a note; double-click a note to edit it. Furniture labels — text, position, size, bold and colour — are set in the panel under the selected item; “Sizes” shows width × depth in a chosen corner.
help.cable.title: Cables:
help.cable.text: Cable tool → click to place points anywhere; double-click, Enter or a click on the last point finishes, Esc cancels; Shift keeps 45° steps. Points snap to furniture (e.g. a switch), walls and other cables. Select a cable to set its colour, label, width and length display; drag it or its points; double-click a segment to add a point, a point to remove it. A cable end placed on an item (socket, switch, desk) is connected to it: it moves with the item, and the item's label becomes From / To unless you type your own. Over a small item (socket, switch) the end snaps to its centre. To run one cable past several consumers, select it and press Continue (branch icon), click the point on the cable to continue from and draw on — the new part belongs to the same cable, and the cable is labelled once: start → every consumer in order. Attach (link icon) makes an already drawn cable a continuation of another one. Drag a straight part of a selected cable to move it sideways (the ends stay); it sticks to parallel cables and trays nearby, so cables can share one path.
help.wiring.title: Wiring mode:
help.wiring.text: the Wiring button dims the plan and switches to a second layer: cables, trays, sockets, rulers and texts added here are shown only in Wiring mode. Tray tool → draw a cable tray like a cable; cables drawn near it snap onto it. Hover a tray to see the cables in it. Each cable can have From / To (e.g. Server room → Desk 1). Any object can be moved between layers from its panel. In the object panel, Layer = Plan / Wiring / Both plans (e.g. a socket shown on both). Settings (in Wiring mode) set the cable width, label sizes, which labels are shown and how bright the plan stays. Groups: cables can be put into groups of this floor or common to all floors (chips in the cable panel); the bulb highlights a group. Tidy lays the cables out at right angles, merges close parallel runs and puts them on trays.
help.gaps.title: Free space:
help.gaps.text: with “Gaps” on, the selected item shows the distance to the nearest wall or furniture on each side; less than 60 cm is highlighted. Items snap flush (0 cm) to walls and neighbours when dragged close — hold Alt to place freely.
help.pan.title: Pan / zoom:
help.pan.text: drag empty space (or drag with the right button) to pan, scroll wheel to zoom; on touch screens drag empty space or use two fingers.
help.group.title: Groups:
help.group.text: Ctrl/Shift+click adds or removes an item; Ctrl/Shift+drag on empty space selects with a frame; drag any selected item to move the whole group; Ctrl+A selects everything; arrow keys move the selection by 1 cm (with Shift — 10 cm).
help.walledit.title: Edit walls and rulers:
help.walledit.text: click a wall to change its type, thickness and length, or drag it to move; click a ruler line to change its length or drag it, drag its ends to adjust.
help.heights.title: Heights:
help.heights.text: in Wiring mode set the room height (Settings), the mounting height of items (e.g. AC 300 cm, panel 160 cm), tray heights (a socket standing in a tray takes the tray's height) and, for a cable, the run height or the height of single points (e.g. up over a wardrobe and down into a tray). Cable lengths add the runs up and down. A cable with "in trays" turned off runs on its own: Tidy doesn't put it into trays.
help.snap.title: Snap:
help.keys.title: Keyboard:
help.keys.text: Esc — Select tool; Ctrl+S — quick save; Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z — undo / redo; Ctrl+C / V / X — copy / paste / cut; Delete — remove selected.
